absent: Vendor-specific implementations of skip, privilege lookup, segment base, register cache and nested intercept decisions are not shown.
Full layouts and lifetimes of vCPU, PMU, PMC, filter and memslot objects beyond accessed fields are not shown.
Handling of event, triple-fault, PMI and PMU requests after they are raised is not shown.
Debug file operation tables and error paths beyond value reporting are not shown.
Counter width, mediation state transitions and reprogramming side effects beyond marker and request are not shown.
CPUID leaf contents and capability derivation beyond family, model, stepping and listed feature checks are not shown.

findings.text: Two public queuing helpers expose exception injection: one carries a numeric vector plus an error code, the other carries a numeric vector plus a payload value. Both forward to a shared multiple-exception coordinator.

Exception state moves from idle to pending with injected clear. A new report while one is pending or injected is classified; contributory pairs and page-fault followed by non-benign synthesize a double-fault vector after clearing old state, otherwise the old report is replaced. A pending double fault followed by another report raises a triple-fault request. Guest-mode reports that the nested layer wants to intercept are diverted to a separate VM-exit record instead.

Vectors are grouped into three classes: page fault alone forms its own class, five divide, segment and state vectors form the contributory class, and all other vectors are benign. The grouping drives double-fault synthesis decisions.
Both the normal exception slot and the nested VM-exit slot keep the same logical record: numeric vector, pending flag, injected flag, error-code presence plus value, and payload presence plus value.

CPUID faulting is active when either the misc-features enable bit for CPUID fault or the HWCR user-disable bit is set. CPUID execution is then permitted only in system management mode or at privilege zero; with faulting disabled it is always permitted.

A guest physical address is legal when no reserved bits defined per vCPU are set. Aligned legality adds an alignment check. Page address validity is aligned legality at page granularity. CR3 legality first strips LAM mask bits when the guest supports LAM, then applies GPA legality.

Family, model and stepping are derived from leaf one; absence of that leaf yields negative one. Intel compatibility is defined as not AMD compatible, and model consistency compares the host boot model against the guest model.

A helper restricted at build time to the XSAVES feature looks up the CPUID leaf implied by that feature, extracts the relevant register, and tests the feature bit, returning false when leaf or register is missing. It consults raw guest CPUID rather than derived capabilities.

Paravirtual feature presence is unconditional when enforcement is off, otherwise it tests a bit in the per-vCPU feature mask. Spec-control MSR presence follows any of four speculation features, and prediction-command MSR presence follows any of three related features. A CPU capability is set only when the boot CPU has it.

Skipping an emulated instruction first delegates to the vendor skip operation; failure returns zero without further effects. Success records a retired instruction for the PMU, then when the pre-skip flags had the trap bit set it injects a single-step debug report and returns that result.

Emulated debug injection has two exits: with hardware-breakpoint or single-step debugging active it fills the run block debug fields and program counter and requests a debug exit to userspace with zero status; otherwise it queues a debug vector with payload and returns one.

Linear instruction pointer is zero when guest state is protected. Otherwise in 64-bit mode it equals the RIP register, while in legacy mode it adds the code-segment base truncated to 32 bits to RIP. Long mode follows the LMA flag on 64-bit builds and is always false otherwise; 64-bit mode additionally requires the code-segment L bit.

Retired-instruction notification forwards a per-PMU bitmap of interested counters. Triggering returns early on an empty bitmap, otherwise intersects with global control when that control exists. It then walks set counters under SRCU, skipping disallowed or privilege-mismatched entries, and increments the rest.

General-purpose allow decisions test include and exclude lists: presence in includes without presence in excludes selects the configured action, absence selects the opposite action. Matching locates the event-select group by binary search over entries sorted by that field, then scans both directions for a masked umask match. Fixed counters test a bitmap bit against the configured allow or deny action. Absence of any filter allows all events.

Without a mediated PMU the increment path bumps a software emulated count and requests reprogramming. With mediation it increments the architectural counter masked to width; a wrap to zero sets the global status bit for that index and, when interrupt-on-overflow is enabled for the counter type, raises a PMI request. Interrupt enable comes from the event-select flag for general counters and from the fixed-control subfield for fixed counters.

Recalculation clears both software counting markers for the counter, then without consulting event filters checks local enablement. When enabled it sets the instructions marker on event match for retired instructions and the branches marker on match for retired branch instructions. Event match ignores edge, pin, counter-mask and in-transaction differences by masking.

Fixed counters are locally enabled when their fixed-control subfield requests kernel or user counting. General counters require the enable flag and, only when the counter advertises mode-specific enables, require that the current mode is not disabled. Fixed type is identified by a dedicated type value.

Privilege matching reads operating-system and user selectors from event-select for general counters and from fixed control for fixed counters. When both selectors agree the result equals that value without reading privilege level; otherwise privilege zero selects the operating-system value and nonzero selects the user value.

Per-vCPU debug files always include guest mode and TSC offset; a LAPIC timer advance file appears only with in-kernel LAPIC, and scaling ratio plus fractional-bits files appear only when TSC control is supported. Each file reports a single 64-bit value from vCPU or capability state.

Reverse-map statistics first test for map presence, then acquire the slots mutex followed by the MMU write lock while walking address spaces, slots and page levels. Locks are released in reverse order before formatting output.
PMU event triggering holds an SRCU read lock across the per-counter walk so the event filter pointer can be dereferenced safely; the lock is released after the walk completes.
A 64-bit sentinel with all bits set marks a CPUID index as not significant.
Reverse-map histograms use eleven logarithmic buckets and three level labels for small, medium and large pages in increasing size order.

Public helpers expose linear RIP lookup, retired-instruction accounting, per-counter emulation recalculation, per-vCPU debug file creation, and a predicate for whether memory slots currently carry reverse maps.
A reverse-map count whose logarithm reaches the bucket limit is clamped to the last bucket with a one-time warning, so very large counts lose precision rather than overflowing the histogram.
Finalizing CPU capabilities warns when configuration was not in progress and then marks configuration as finished.
Slots are considered to have reverse maps when the TDP MMU is disabled or when a shadow root has been allocated.
The CPUID header uses an include guard and the debug source prefixes log text with the module name.
